learning_outcomes.text: Critical sense, respect for diversity and social focus of professional activity related to energy management.
Comprehension of the links between development and energy sector technologies and businesses.
Analysis of concrete cases of basic need dissatisfaction and design of solutions based on electric power management systems.
Acquire a supportive and global vision of reality, complementing conventional technical learning with ethical principles that should guide their professional career.
Analytical sense with respect to the diversity and social focus of the professional activity related to the management of energy.
Comprehension of the links between development and energy sector technologies and businesses.
Analysis of concrete cases of basic need dissatisfaction and design of solutions based on electric power management systems.

syllabus_topics: Cooperation for development: methods and agents
Electric power systems to promote (or to prevent) development
Projects of cooperation for the development with a high component of electric power
Off-grid power - electrical energy in rural communities
Micro/pico hydropower in various countries for communities not connected to the grid

assessment_methods.method: Assessable practice 1.1 (P1.1): individual or group assignment applying part of the content of topic 1
Assessable practice 1.2 (P1.2): individual or group assignment applying part of the content of topic 1
Assessable practice 1.3 (P1.3): individual or group assignment applying part of the content of topic 1
Assessable practice 1.4 (P1.4): individual or group assignment applying part of the content of topic 1
Assessable practice 2 (P2): individual or group task applying the content of topic 2
Attendance and active participation in the classroom (AP)
Assessable practice 3 (P3): individual or group task applying the content of topic 3
Assessable practice 4 (P4): individual or group assignment applying the content of topic 4

assessment_rules: The final grade for the ordinary assessment is calculated as (P1.1 + P1.2 + P1.3 + P1.4 + P2 + AP) x 1/9 + (P3 x 0.8 + P4 x 0.2) x 1/3. The subject is passed if the formula yields at least 5 points. For extraordinary assessment, students must contact the coordinator at least one month before the exam to receive equivalent tasks, with the formula being (P1.1 + P1.2 + P1.3 + P1.4 + P2) x 2/15 + (P3 x 0.8 + P4 x 0.2) x 1/3, and a minimum of 5 points to pass. There are no minimum marks for individual practices.
